questions.stem: WHY does the SKY appear BLUE?

options.option_text: Absorption of blue by water vapour

questions.explanation: RAYLEIGH SCATTERING — when SUNLIGHT enters the atmosphere, it is scattered by molecules (and small particles) whose size is much SMALLER than the wavelength of light. Rayleigh showed that the INTENSITY of scattering is INVERSELY PROPORTIONAL to the FOURTH POWER of the wavelength (I ∝ 1/λ⁴). Since BLUE (λ ≈ 470 nm) has a much shorter wavelength than RED (λ ≈ 650 nm), blue is scattered ~(650/470)⁴ ≈ 3.7× MORE than red. Violet is scattered even more, but (1) the Sun emits less violet, and (2) our eyes are less sensitive to violet than blue → net result, we perceive a BLUE sky. WHY IS THE SUNRISE / SUNSET RED-ORANGE? At those times the Sun is low on the horizon, so light travels through a LONGER atmospheric path. By the time light reaches us, most of the blue has been scattered away — leaving the longer (red/orange) wavelengths dominant. WHY IS DEEP SEA / SKY-AT-NIGHT DARK? No atmosphere to scatter (space above) — starry field dominates. WHY DOES THE SUN LOOK WHITE AT NOON? Overhead path is shortest → minimal scattering of any colour → all wavelengths reach you. WHY CLOUDS ARE WHITE? Water droplets in clouds are MUCH BIGGER than light wavelength → cause MIE SCATTERING (wavelength-independent), scattering all colours equally → white. WHY DANGER SIGNALS ARE RED? Red has longest visible wavelength → least scattered by air/dust/fog → visible farthest. WHY MILK IS WHITE? Suspension of fat globules — Mie scattering of all colours. atmospheric molecules (N₂, O₂) scatter SHORTER wavelengths (blue) about 5-6× more than longer wavelengths (red); ∝ 1/λ⁴.

questions.stem: MYOPIA (short-sightedness), where a person cannot see DISTANT objects clearly, is corrected by using:
questions.explanation: MYOPIA (Greek ‘myo’ = ‘shut’; also called NEAR-SIGHTEDNESS / SHORT-SIGHTEDNESS) — the eye can see NEAR objects clearly but DISTANT objects appear blurred. CAUSE: (a) eyeball is too ELONGATED front-to-back, OR (b) cornea/lens curvature too strong — so that parallel light rays from distant objects converge to a focal point BEFORE the retina, giving a blurred image on the retina. CORRECTION: CONCAVE LENS (also called DIVERGING / MINUS-power lens) — diverges incoming rays slightly so they focus further back, landing exactly on the retina. Power of lens: NEGATIVE (e.g., -2.5 D). HYPERMETROPIA (far-sightedness) — opposite — distant OK but near objects blurred. Cause: eyeball too SHORT, so image forms BEHIND the retina. Correction: CONVEX / CONVERGING / PLUS-power lens (+ve D). PRESBYOPIA — age-related loss of flexibility of crystalline lens (usually after age 40); need BIFOCAL or progressive lenses. ASTIGMATISM — cornea/lens has unequal curvature in different meridians (oval instead of spherical), causing blurred/distorted vision; corrected by CYLINDRICAL LENS. CATARACT — opacification of the crystalline lens; treated by SURGICAL removal + insertion of Intraocular Lens (IOL). HUMAN EYE: near-point ~25 cm (‘least distance of distinct vision’); far-point = infinity; pupil diameter 2-8 mm; retina has RODS (120 million, B&W / low light) + CONES (6-7 million, colour — R, G, B); blind spot (optic disc, no photoreceptors); FOVEA CENTRALIS (sharpest vision). it moves the image BACKWARD onto the retina by diverging incoming parallel rays.

questions.stem: The phenomenon by which we see a RAINBOW requires:

options.option_text: DISPERSION + REFRACTION + TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION of sunlight in water droplets; observer stands with back to Sun; primary rainbow ~42° angle, red outside, violet inside

questions.explanation: RAINBOW — formed by the combined interaction of SUNLIGHT with tiny WATER DROPLETS in the atmosphere (after rain); the formation involves THREE phenomena: (1) REFRACTION — sunlight enters water droplet, is bent (dense medium → less speed → bending toward normal); (2) DISPERSION — the 7 colours of white light bend by DIFFERENT amounts (violet most, red least) because refractive index n(violet) > n(red) — splits into VIBGYOR; (3) TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION — at the back surface of the droplet, rays reflect internally; (4) REFRACTION again upon exit. The net effect: each colour emerges at a slightly different angle; red at ~42° above anti-solar point, violet at ~40°. Thus a PRIMARY RAINBOW = semicircular arc at ~42° radius centred on the ANTI-SOLAR POINT (point opposite the Sun from observer). RED on the OUTER arc, VIOLET on the INNER. OBSERVER must stand with their BACK to the Sun, Sun behind them. SECONDARY RAINBOW — fainter, larger arc at ~51° radius; formed by TWO internal reflections; COLOUR ORDER REVERSED (red inside, violet outside). Between primary and secondary: ALEXANDER'S DARK BAND (less light scattered). On a 360° horizon (from an aeroplane) you can see a full circular rainbow. MNEMONIC for order: VIBGYOR (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red). NEWTON, 1666, performed the CLASSIC PRISM EXPERIMENT — split sunlight into colours + recombined them → proved white light = mixture of all colours. PRISMATIC dispersion is the BASIS of SPECTROMETERS.

questions.stem: A CONCAVE MIRROR is used in:

options.option_text: SHAVING MIRRORS, CAR/TORCH HEADLIGHTS, DENTIST'S MIRROR, SOLAR COOKERS, REFLECTING TELESCOPES

questions.explanation: CONCAVE (CONVERGING) MIRROR — a mirror whose reflecting surface CURVES INWARD (like the inside of a spoon). Properties: (1) Parallel rays converge at the FOCAL POINT (F). (2) Image characteristics depend on object distance: (a) object BEYOND C (centre of curvature) → image real, inverted, DIMINISHED; (b) object AT C → same-size, real, inverted; (c) object BETWEEN F and C → real, inverted, MAGNIFIED; (d) object AT F → image at infinity; (e) object BETWEEN POLE and F → VIRTUAL, ERECT, MAGNIFIED. USES: (1) SHAVING / MAKEUP MIRROR — face within F → magnified erect image. (2) DENTIST'S MIRROR — small tooth within F → enlarged view. (3) TORCH / HEADLIGHT / SEARCHLIGHT REFLECTOR — bulb placed AT F → reflected light emerges as parallel beam. (4) SOLAR COOKER / SOLAR CONCENTRATOR — parallel sunlight converges at F → intense heat. (5) REFLECTING TELESCOPE (NEWTONIAN, CASSEGRAIN) — parabolic concave mirror used as primary; avoids chromatic aberration of lenses (faced by REFRACTING telescopes like Galilean/Keplerian). MIRROR FORMULA: 1/v + 1/u = 1/f (v = image distance, u = object distance, f = focal length). MAGNIFICATION m = -v/u = h'/h. NEWTON'S CARTESIAN SIGN CONVENTION: distances measured from pole; positive to the right, negative to the left (typically). For CONCAVE mirror, f < 0 (if light travels left-to-right conventionally). CONVEX (DIVERGING) mirror uses: REAR-VIEW (wider field, diminished image always), SECURITY/SHOP mirrors, STREET light reflectors. PLANE mirrors: image same size, erect, virtual, laterally inverted, distance = object distance. because it forms a MAGNIFIED / ERECT image when object is within focal length, and a PARALLEL BEAM when source is at focus.

questions.stem: The phenomenon where LIGHT bends AROUND edges of an obstacle/slit is called:
questions.explanation: DIFFRACTION — the BENDING of waves around the corners of an obstacle or through an aperture; a phenomenon distinctive of WAVES (NOT particles). Light diffraction is usually small because visible wavelength (~500 nm) is much shorter than everyday obstacles, but becomes noticeable with slits/gaps of comparable size. HISTORIC EXPERIMENTS: (1) FRANCESCO GRIMALDI (1660s) — first observed + named ‘diffractio’; light passing through small aperture shows fringes of dark/light (not pure geometric shadow). (2) THOMAS YOUNG (1801) — famous DOUBLE-SLIT EXPERIMENT: sunlight through two parallel narrow slits produces an INTERFERENCE pattern of bright & dark fringes on a screen; proved WAVE nature of light (Newton had argued it was corpuscular). Formula: bright fringes at d·sinθ = n·λ. (3) FRESNEL, FRAUNHOFER — further developed diffraction theory. (4) X-RAY DIFFRACTION — Von Laue (1912), Bragg (father+son, 1913) — discovered X-rays diffracted through crystals obey nλ = 2d·sinθ; basis of crystallography (e.g., Watson-Crick DNA 1953 using Rosalind Franklin's X-ray data). RELATED optics phenomena: INTERFERENCE (superposition of two coherent waves → constructive/destructive); POLARIZATION (confining wave oscillations to one plane — only transverse waves can be polarized, so light can but sound cannot); TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION (at interface with a less dense medium beyond critical angle — basis of OPTICAL FIBRES, DIAMONDS' sparkle, MIRAGE). WAVE-PARTICLE DUALITY of light: Newton said particle; Young diffraction said wave; Einstein's photoelectric effect (1905, Nobel 1921) said particle (PHOTONS); Quantum mechanics unifies both — light is BOTH. de Broglie (1924) extended to matter waves. most pronounced when the obstacle/slit size is comparable to the wavelength of light; YOUNG’s double-slit experiment (1801) proved wave nature of light.

questions.stem: A MIRAGE (the shimmering ‘water on hot desert road’ illusion) is caused by:

options.option_text: TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION of light + refraction by layers of AIR of differing densities

questions.explanation: MIRAGE — an OPTICAL PHENOMENON caused by the REFRACTION and TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION of light as it passes through LAYERS of AIR with different DENSITIES (and hence different refractive indices). MECHANISM (inferior mirage — common on hot desert roads): (1) Near the SURFACE, air is hot → EXPANDED → LESS DENSE → LOWER REFRACTIVE INDEX. (2) Higher up, air is cooler → DENSER → HIGHER index. (3) Light rays from the sky travelling obliquely downward PASS from denser → rarer layers progressively. (4) When the angle of incidence exceeds the critical angle in any layer, TOTAL INTERNAL REFLECTION occurs → rays bend upward again. (5) To the observer, these bent rays LOOK LIKE they came from a point on the ground → image of sky appears on the road surface, resembling WATER / REFLECTION. Inverted images of distant objects (trees, cars) may also appear. TWO TYPES: (a) INFERIOR MIRAGE — image appears BELOW the real object (classic desert/road mirage). (b) SUPERIOR MIRAGE — image appears ABOVE the real object; seen over cold seas/ice (POLAR regions) — this is the origin of the ‘FLYING DUTCHMAN’ ghost ship, the ‘FATA MORGANA’ of the Straits of Messina, and ‘looming’ effects. MORE OPTICAL PHENOMENA of refraction through atmosphere: (1) APPARENT POSITION of stars / Sun DIFFERS from real position (we see Sun 2 minutes BEFORE it rises and 2 minutes AFTER it sets due to atmospheric refraction, so the ‘day’ is 4 min longer than geometric). (2) TWINKLING OF STARS — atmospheric turbulence causes rapid refractive index changes; planets (extended disks) twinkle less. (3) CIRCULAR/OVAL appearance of Sun-Moon near horizon — differential refraction of top vs bottom. (4) REFRACTION at air-glass-water interfaces makes pencils look bent in water, letters appear displaced under glass slab, swimming pools look shallower than they are. hot/less dense air near the ground refracts light upward, bending images of the sky.

questions.stem: The PRIMARY colours of LIGHT (ADDITIVE) are:
questions.explanation: PRIMARY COLOURS OF LIGHT — RGB (Red-Green-Blue). Known as ADDITIVE primaries because adding them gives brighter colours (up to white). This is how TV screens, computer monitors, phones, LED displays work — millions of tiny pixels, each having R, G, B sub-pixels of controlled intensity. ADDITIVE COMBINATIONS: R + G = YELLOW; G + B = CYAN; R + B = MAGENTA; R + G + B = WHITE. These combinations (C, M, Y) are called SECONDARY colours of light. HUMAN colour VISION — retina has 3 types of CONE cells (photoreceptors) sensitive to roughly RED (L, long wavelength), GREEN (M, medium), BLUE (S, short). Brain combines signals to perceive colour. Colour-blindness (Daltonism) usually = defect in one cone type (most commonly red-green). Wavelength ranges: RED ~625-750 nm, GREEN ~500-565, BLUE ~450-485. SUBTRACTIVE PRIMARIES — CYAN, MAGENTA, YELLOW (CMY) or CMYK (with blacK) — basis of PRINTING and PAINT. Subtractive because pigments ABSORB some wavelengths and REFLECT only a subset. CMY combinations: C + M = Blue; M + Y = Red; C + Y = Green; C + M + Y = Black (in theory; in practice muddy-brown, hence K). In paint, PRIMARY colours traditionally taught to children are RED-YELLOW-BLUE — but strictly CMY is the scientifically correct subtractive primaries. The colour of AN OBJECT depends on which wavelengths it reflects (absorbs others): a red apple absorbs all light except red wavelengths, reflecting red. A BLACK object absorbs all; WHITE reflects all. In darkness, objects have NO colour (no light to reflect). OPPONENT-PROCESS THEORY (Hering): colour vision also processed as R-G, B-Y, and black-white pairs in neural pathways. basis of TV/monitor pixels, human colour vision (cones), additive mixing produces White when all three overlap.

options.option_text: LIGHT AMPLIFICATION by STIMULATED EMISSION of RADIATION
Linear Array of Shining Electron Rays

questions.explanation: LASER (acronym) — Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Concept predicted by EINSTEIN (1917, stimulated emission theory). First MASER (Microwave amplification by stimulated emission) built by Charles Townes (1953). First LASER built by THEODORE MAIMAN (1960, ruby laser, USA). Nobel for laser-adjacent work — Townes, Basov, Prokhorov 1964; Schawlow 1981; Ashkin, Mourou, Strickland 2018 (chirped pulse amplification); Abacus (2023) for attosecond. PROPERTIES: (1) MONOCHROMATIC — single wavelength (very narrow spectral width); (2) COHERENT — all photons in-phase (spatial + temporal coherence); (3) HIGHLY DIRECTIONAL — very little divergence (can travel km with minimal spread); (4) VERY HIGH INTENSITY (concentrated energy, can reach terawatts in pulsed mode); (5) polarised. MECHANISM: (a) active medium (ruby, He-Ne, semiconductor, CO₂, Nd:YAG, dye, free-electron, fibre); (b) pumping source (flashlamp, electric discharge, another laser) excites atoms to higher energy states → POPULATION INVERSION; (c) when an excited atom is hit by a photon of the right wavelength, it undergoes STIMULATED EMISSION — releases a photon identical in phase, direction, wavelength; (d) mirrors in a RESONANT CAVITY amplify this into a coherent beam; (e) one mirror is partially transparent, letting the beam exit. TYPES of lasers by ACTIVE MEDIUM: (i) SOLID-STATE — Ruby, Nd:YAG, Ti:Sapphire, Fiber. (ii) GAS — He-Ne, CO₂ (cutting metals), Argon, Excimer (eye surgery). (iii) LIQUID — Dye lasers. (iv) SEMICONDUCTOR — Laser diode (CD/DVD/Blu-ray, fibre-optic comms, pointers). USES: FIBRE-OPTIC communication, BARCODE scanners, BLUE-RAY/DVD/CD readers, LIDAR, SURGERY (LASIK eye surgery, cancer ablation, angioplasty), INDUSTRY (cutting, welding, 3D printing, marking), MILITARY (range-finding, directed-energy weapons), SCIENTIFIC research (spectroscopy, laser cooling to microkelvin), HOLOGRAPHY, light shows, GRAVITATIONAL WAVE DETECTION (LIGO). a device producing a coherent, monochromatic, highly directional beam of light.

questions.stem: The COLOUR of a BLUE OBJECT under BLUE LIGHT will appear:
questions.explanation: COLOURED OBJECTS under DIFFERENT COLOURED LIGHTS — key principle: an object appears the colour of the LIGHT IT REFLECTS. A blue object ABSORBS red, orange, yellow, green, indigo, violet and REFLECTS BLUE. Under WHITE LIGHT (containing all colours), you see its reflected blue → it looks blue. Under MONOCHROMATIC BLUE LIGHT, the only wavelength available is blue — which the object does reflect → still appears BLUE. Under MONOCHROMATIC RED LIGHT, only red is available; but the blue object ABSORBS red → no reflection → appears BLACK. A WHITE OBJECT reflects all wavelengths → looks the COLOUR of the incident light (blue under blue light, red under red light, white under white). A BLACK OBJECT absorbs all → appears BLACK under any illumination. ADDITIONAL EXAMPLES (tested often): (1) A red flower under green light → looks BLACK. (2) A yellow shirt under red light → looks RED (yellow reflects red+green; red alone reflects → red; hence it appears red — tricky! Need to think: yellow = reflects both red and green). (3) A yellow shirt under blue light → looks BLACK (yellow absorbs blue). (4) Rose in magenta light → looks BRIGHT RED/MAGENTA (rose reflects red; magenta = red+blue; red reflected, blue absorbed → red). COLOUR FILTER principle — a RED filter lets only red light through, absorbing others. A PIECE OF WHITE PAPER seen through red+green filters stacked → dark (neither red nor green passes both). COLOUR CONSTANCY — the human brain's remarkable ability to perceive an object's colour as roughly constant under different illuminations; the brain uses context + white-balance. Famous test: ‘THE DRESS’ (2015 internet phenomenon — blue/black vs white/gold due to perceived white balance). because the object is reflecting the blue wavelength (it only reflects blue; since blue is available in incident light, it remains visible).

questions.stem: The SPEED OF LIGHT in VACUUM is approximately:
questions.explanation: SPEED OF LIGHT in vacuum (c) — EXACTLY 299,792,458 m/s (by definition since 1983; used to DEFINE the metre: ‘the distance light travels in 1/299,792,458 seconds’). Approximate value: 3 × 10⁸ m/s = 3 × 10⁵ km/s = 3,00,000 km/s. Light takes: (a) 1.3 seconds from Moon to Earth (384,400 km away); (b) 8 minutes 20 seconds from Sun (150 million km / 1 AU); (c) 4.2 years from nearest star PROXIMA CENTAURI; (d) 8 min 20 s from the Sun, so when you SEE the Sun, you're seeing it as it was 8 min ago; (e) 100,000 years to cross the Milky Way galaxy; (f) 2.5 million years to reach us from Andromeda. SPEED depends on MEDIUM — in a MEDIUM, light slows down: v = c/n, where n = REFRACTIVE INDEX. Typical n: VACUUM = 1.000; AIR ~1.0003 (nearly vacuum); WATER ~1.33; GLASS ~1.50; DIAMOND ~2.42 (very high, hence brilliant sparkle due to total internal reflection); ICE = 1.31. In DIAMOND, light travels at ~1.24 × 10⁸ m/s (less than half c). HISTORICAL MEASUREMENTS: (1) OLE RØMER (1676) — first estimation using Jupiter's moon IO eclipses; got ~2.2 × 10⁸ m/s. (2) JAMES BRADLEY (1729) — stellar aberration; 3.01 × 10⁸. (3) ARMAND FIZEAU (1849) — toothed wheel method; 3.13 × 10⁸. (4) LEON FOUCAULT (1862) — rotating mirror; 2.98 × 10⁸. (5) ALBERT MICHELSON (1879 onward, multiple) — rotating prism, interferometer; won NOBEL 1907 for these measurements. SPECIAL RELATIVITY (EINSTEIN 1905) — c is the ULTIMATE SPEED LIMIT for information, matter, energy; c is INVARIANT in every inertial frame — foundational principle. E = mc². NOTHING can travel faster than c in vacuum (though phase velocity, group velocity, and apparent superluminal effects exist in special cases without transmitting info faster than c). i.e., 3,00,000 km/s = 3 × 10⁸ m/s.
